claims.text: Role in GCA: low-dose ASA (81 to 100 mg PO QD) may help prevent ischemic events; consider it w critical or flow-limiting vertebral or carotid involvement.
claims.quote: Low-dose aspirin (81 to 100 mg orally once a day) may help prevent ischemic events and should be considered for patients who have critical or flow-limiting involvement of the vertebral or carotid arteries.
The concurrent use of aspirin with other NSAID's should be avoided because this may increase bleeding or lead to decreased renal function.
Patients on anticoagulation therapy are at increased risk for bleeding
Avoid aspirin in patients with severe renal failure (glomerular filtration rate less than 10 mL/minute).
Avoid aspirin in patients with severe hepatic insufficiency.

claims.text: Counseling: three or more alcoholic drinks a day raises the bleed risk.
claims.quote: Patients who consume three or more alcoholic drinks every day should be counseled about the bleeding risks involved with chronic, heavy alcohol use while taking aspirin.

claims.text: Toxicity (salicylism): early N/V, tinnitus and hypervent;
claims.quote: With acute overdose, early symptoms include nausea, vomiting, tinnitus, and hyperventilation.
Salicylate poisoning causes respiratory alkalosis and, by an independent mechanism, metabolic acidosis.

claims.text: which eventually becomes the primary finding.
claims.quote: Eventually, usually as salicylate levels decrease, poorly compensated or uncompensated metabolic acidosis is the primary finding.

claims.text: Tx w activated charcoal and alkaline diuresis w extra KCl;
claims.quote: Treat with activated charcoal and alkaline diuresis with extra KCl.
Consider hemodialysis if poisoning is severe.
